elements.element: Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence.
elements.evidence: Inserted Insurance clause: "(a) commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate".

elements.element: Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate.
elements.evidence: Same limb (a) expressly states "USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate".

elements.element: Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: Limb (b): "professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000".

elements.element: If Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 5,000,000.
elements.evidence: Limb (c): "where IBM processes any data belonging to, supplied by, or processed on behalf of Customer, cyber and privacy liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000" — the trigger reaches every category of Customer data rather than selected named data types, which is required here because "Customer Data" is not a defined term in this Agreement.

elements.element: Vendor maintains workers' compensation coverage as required by law.
elements.evidence: Limb (d): "workers' compensation insurance as required by law".

elements.element: Vendor provides certificates of insurance on request.
elements.evidence: Final sentence: "IBM shall provide certificates of insurance on request."

elements.element: Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: E&O of "not less than USD 2,000,000" exceeds the USD 1,000,000 fallback floor.

elements.element: Cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: Cyber and privacy liability of "not less than USD 5,000,000" exceeds the USD 2,000,000 fallback floor.

reasons: The finding is correctly classified as missing: the cited paragraphs (5.3 security disclaimer, 14.12 risk of loss, 14.18 data protection, notices) contain no coverage undertaking anywhere, and IBM hosts the e-business Hosting Environment and processes personal information on Customer's behalf, so the absence of insurance is walk-away territory under the rule.
All six preferred elements are met in operative language by the single inserted Insurance section; no element is merely promised in the margin comment.

Minimality is satisfied: the insertion is a concise single paragraph limited to the six checklist items. The drafter correctly omitted the model language's extras ("at its own expense" and the "throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter" survival tail), which are not required by any selected element and would have failed minimality. No existing words were deleted or paraphrased.

Intent is preserved: nothing in the retained text (risk of loss allocation in 14.12, the security disclaimer in 5.3, or the data protection wording in 14.18) is contradicted or rendered inconsistent, and the new section introduces no undefined term or dangling cross-reference — the cyber trigger deliberately avoids relying on the undefined phrase "Customer Data" by describing the data categories directly.
The fallback level is independently satisfied because the preferred limits exceed the fallback floors, so the position is complete at both levels.
No action required from the drafter; the redline as rendered is position-complete at the preferred level.
